# Adjudication Task — Chapter 287

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃287화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나, 임꺽정, 송송이와 김 집사.
  6|
  7|그러나 병실로 들어선 이정룡의 시선은 오직 한 사람에게 고정되어 있었다.
  8|
  9|바로 최 팀장이었다.
 10|
 11|“많이 컸구나.”
 12|
 13|“……!”
 14|
 15|이정룡의 첫 마디를 듣는 순간, 쇠망치로 뒤통수를 한 대 맞은 듯한 기분이 들었다.
 16|
 17|이거였다. 최 팀장이 숨긴 것이.
 18|
 19|직장 상사와의 단순한 상하 관계가 아닌 게 분명했다.
 20|
 21|‘내가 알기로 최 팀장이 아레스 길드에 몸담았던 기간은 삼사 년 남짓.’
 22|
 23|아무리 적게 잡아도 이십 대 초중반 때 이정룡을 만났을 것이다. 그런 그에게 많이 컸다는 말은 어울리지 않는다.
 24|
 25|그건 부모님 친구나 명절날 친척들에게서나 듣는 소리니까.
 26|
 27|“오랜만에 뵙습니다. 이정룡 부길드장님.”
 28|
 29|딱딱한 호칭과 말투. 이정룡이 흥미롭다는 눈빛으로 최 팀장을 응시했다.
 30|
 31|“부길드장님이라, 네가 어렸을 때는 나를 할아버지라 불렀었지.”
 32|
 33|할아버지라고?
 34|
 35|두 번째 충격이다. 순간 혹시? 하는 생각이 들었지만 이내 머릿속에서 지웠다.
 36|
 37|이건 단순한 호칭 문제다. 어린 마음에 할아버지라 불렀을 뿐, 이정룡이 최 팀장의 진짜 할아버지는 아닐 것이다.
 38|
 39|‘최 팀장이 어렸을 때부터 긴밀한 관계가 있었던 건 확실해 보이는데.’
 40|
 41|이정룡과 그런 사이였다는 것만으로도 이미 보통이 아니다.
 42|
 43|모두가 놀라는 가운데 평정심을 유지하고 있는 사람은 김 집사와 침착하게 대답하는 최 팀장뿐이었다.
 44|
 45|“그랬었지요. 20년 전에는.”
 46|
 47|“세월이 무섭구나. 그렇게 애교 많던 꼬마 녀석이 이렇게 변할 줄이야.”
 48|
 49|“갈수록 보이지 않던 것들이 점점 보이더군요.”
 50|
 51|“작년에 사표를 냈다는 보고는 받았다. 곰곰이 생각해 보니 네가 길드에 들어온 후 얼굴 한 번 본 적 없더구나. 내심 아쉽다는 생각이 들었지.”
 52|
 53|말과는 달리 전혀 아쉬운 표정이 아니다. 대답하는 최 팀장 역시 마찬가지였다.
 54|
 55|“저도 마찬가집니다. 본사에는 발도 들이지 못하게 바로 해외 발령만 안 내셨다면 자주 뵐 수 있었을 텐데요.”
 56|
 57|“왜, 해외 지사가 마음에 들지 않더냐?”
 58|
 59|“제가 있을 곳이 아니라고 느꼈습니다. 그뿐입니다.”
 60|
 61|“있을 곳이 아니다…….”
 62|
 63|“부길드장님께서도 원하신 그림 아닙니까?”
 64|
 65|“내가 말이냐?”
 66|
 67|이정룡이 피식, 웃음을 터트렸다.
 68|
 69|“그래서 새 둥지를 틀었느냐? 남의 이름을 빌려 가면서까지?”
 70|
 71|“말씀하시는데 끼어들어 죄송합니다만.”
 72|
 73|침묵을 지키고 있던 김 집사가 불쑥 입을 열었다. 평소처럼 평온하기 그지없는 목소리다.
 74|
 75|“도련님과 제가 남은 아니지요.”
 76|
 77|“아니, 이게 누군가?”
 78|
 79|이정룡이 짐짓 눈을 크게 떴다.
 80|
 81|다분히 과장된 행동이었다. 최 팀장을 알았다면 그와 가장 가까운 김 집사를 모를 리 없을 테니까.
 82|
 83|“김화종? 화종이 맞지?”
 84|
 85|“오랜만입니다. 선배.”
 86|
 87|김 집사는 이정룡이 내민 손을 거절하지 않았다. 두 사람은 옅은 미소마저 띤 채 악수를 나눴다.
 88|
 89|‘반말? 거기에 선배?’
 90|
 91|두 사람이 정확히 어떤 관계인지는 둘째 치고, 생각 이상으로 친한 사이인 모양이다.
 92|
 93|“직접 오길 잘했군. 우리가 마지막으로 만난 게…… 한 20년쯤 전이던가?”
 94|
 95|“정확히는 18년입니다. 십팔 년.”
 96|
 97|기분 탓인가, 특정 단어에서 혀에 힘이 들어간 것 같은데.
 98|
 99|슬쩍 옆을 돌아보니 송송이와 임꺽정은 귀신이라도 본 것 같은 표정이었다.
100|
101|‘아, 기분 탓이 아니었구나.’
102|
103|생각 이상으로 친하긴 개뿔. 내 눈이 삐었지.
104|
105|정정한다. 김 집사는 이정룡과 친하긴커녕 그를 싫어한다.
106|
107|이정룡은 여전히 웃음을 띤 채 말했다.
108|
109|“화종이 자네, 못 본 사이 신수만 훤해진 줄 알았더니 배짱도 두둑해졌구먼.”
110|
111|의미심장한 한마디였다. 그러나 은은한 압박이 담긴 그의 말에도 김 집사의 눈동자는 흔들리지 않았다.
112|
113|“사람은 마음의 여유가 생기면 신수가 훤해지는 법입니다.”
114|
115|“여유?”
116|
117|“호랑이 아가리에서 도련님을 건져 내니까 속이 후련해지더군요. 배짱은 원래 두둑했고요.”
118|
119|“으하하! 그랬지. 자네는 한 번 마음 먹었다 싶으면 앞뒤 가리지 않았어. 그 물불 가리지 않는 성격 덕분에 나도 목숨을 건졌고.”
120|
121|“기억납니다. 한강.”
122|
123|“그래, 한강. 마포대교가 무너진 날 말일세. 화종이 자네도 아직 기억하는구먼.”
124|
125|“틈만 나면 떠올리고 후회합니다. 그때 선배를 구하지 않았다면 지금 같은 일이 벌어지지는 않았을 테니까요.”
126|
127|다시 정정한다. 김 집사는 이정룡을 싫어하는 것이 아니다.
128|
129|존나게 싫어한다. 차라리 죽었으면 싶을 정도로.
130|
131|마법사라 칼만 안 들었을 뿐, 그의 혓바닥이 칼날이었다.
132|
133|그의 독설에 이정룡의 뒤에 철탑처럼 시립해 있던 석고준이 한 걸음 앞으로 나섰다.
134|
135|“입조심하시지요.”
136|
137|“입조심?”
138|
139|“함부로 대하실 분이 아닙니다.”
140|
141|김 집사가 묘한 눈빛으로 석고준을 바라봤다.
142|
143|“얼핏 봐도 실력이 대단해 보이는데, 헌터님은 성함이 어찌 됩니까?”
144|
145|“부길드장님의 경호를 책임지고 있는 석고준입니다.”
146|
147|“그래요. 석고준 팀장.”
148|
149|김 집사 특유의 중저음이 부드럽게 뒤를 이었다.
150|
151|“할 말 다 했으면 이제 입 닥치고 뒤에 처박혀 있게. 자네 따위가 끼어들 자리가 아니야.”
152|
153|“……!”
154|
155|안 그래도 무표정한 석고준의 얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳었다.
156|
157|놈의 이마 위로 핏줄이 도드라지던 그때, 이정룡이 너털웃음을 터트리며 석고준을 뒤로 물렸다.
158|
159|“나이를 먹어서 온순해졌나 했는데…… 그 성질머리는 여전하군. 그래, 이래야 김화종이지.”
160|
161|“성질머리 고약한 것으로 따지자면 제가 선배님께 몇 수는 접어야지요. 안 그렇습니까?”
162|
163|최 팀장도 서늘한 목소리로 한마디를 보탰다.
164|
165|“쓸모없는 대화는 이쯤하고 본론을 말씀하십시오.”
166|
167|이정룡에게 이렇게 함부로 말할 수 있는 사람이 대한민국에, 아니 세계를 통틀어 몇 명이나 될까?
168|
169|폭풍우가 몰아치는 대화에 임꺽정과 송송이는 입이 딱 벌어졌다.
170|
171|특히 김 집사의 모습은, 몇 달 전 그가 상동 길드장 임춘수를 개처럼 굴리는 모습을 직관한 나조차도 내심 놀랄 정도였다.
172|
173|‘도대체 무슨 일이 있었길래.’
174|
175|최 팀장은 물론이고 김 집사까지. 평소의 모습과 비교하면 달라도 너무 다르다.
176|
177|“한 명은 젊어서 성격이 급하고, 다른 한 명은 젊었을 적 성격을 아직 못 버렸군. 뭐, 슬슬 본론으로 들어가는 것도 나쁘진 않겠지. 먼저 초대받은 입장에서 섭섭하긴 하지만.”
178|
179|“지금 초대라고 했습니까?”
180|
181|“착각하셨군요. 우리 중 부길드장님을 초대할 사람은 아무도 없습니다.”
182|
183|“잘 생각해 보게. 한 명 정도는 있지 않겠나?”
184|
185|두 사람을 재미있다는 듯이 바라보던 이정룡이 돌연 나를 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
186|
187|“저 친구 말이야.”
188|
189|순간 적막이 내리깔렸다.
190|
191|사람들의 시선 속, 잠깐 생각에 잠겨 있던 나는 조심스럽게 입을 열었다.
192|
193|“그게 무슨 개소립니까?”
194|
195|말이 끝나기가 무섭게 석고준이 낮게 으르렁거렸다. 이정룡이 고개를 가로젓지 않았다면 사냥개처럼 달려들었을 기세다.
196|
197|석고준을 제지한 이정룡이 내게 말했다.
198|
199|“자네가 그러지 않았나. 직접 찾아와서 피해자에게 사과하라고.”
200|
201|“아.”
202|
203|분명히 그런 말을 하긴 했었다. 박지훈과 박태섭에게.
204|
205|“정말 올 줄 몰랐다는 표정이로군.”
206|
207|“솔직히 그렇습니다. 여기까지 찾아오다니, 무슨 수작입니까?”
208|
209|“자네는 말을 앞뒤 가리지 않고 내뱉는 경향이 있어. 초대에 응했으니 감사 인사부터 해야 하는 것이 아닌가?”
210|
211|감사 인사?
212|
213|나는 헛웃음을 흘렸다. 뒷말은 하도 어이가 없어 대꾸할 가치조차 느끼지 못했다.
214|
215|“입은 삐뚤어져도 말은 똑바로 하시죠. 초대가 아니라 요구였습니다. 사과 요구.”
216|
217|“아니지. 이곳에 온 것이 내 뜻이 아니었다면, 자네나 평화 길드 따위가 나를 한 걸음이라도 움직이게 할 수 있었을까?”
218|
219|“그건…….”
220|
221|“자네도 그렇게 생각하지 않았나? 정말 올 줄 몰랐다고.”
222|
223|찬물을 뒤집어쓴 기분이었다. 말문이 턱하고 막혔다.
224|
225|그의 말은 전부 사실이었다.
226|
227|가슴으로는 분노와 복수를 외치면서도 이정룡이 올 것이라는 기대는 하지 않았다. 그 와중에 머리는 냉철하게 현실과 타협한 것이다.
228|
229|아레스 길드의 실질적 지배자인 이정룡이라는 거물을, 아직 내 힘으로 이 자리에 무릎 꿇릴 수는 없다고.
230|
231|“요구는 강자의 권리일세. 약자가 강자에게 하는 말은 절대 요구가 될 수 없어. 전부 부탁이고 초대지.”
232|
233|“……!”
234|
235|“그래서 나는 초대를 받아 온 거야. 자네들이 어떤 약점을 쥐고 흔들더라도 그 사실은 변치 않는다네. 나는 이정룡이니까. 내가 아레스 길드이고, 아레스 길드가 곧 나니까.”
236|
237|잔잔하지만 힘이 실린 목소리에 나를 포함한 평화 길드원들은 할 말을 잃었다.
238|
239|적어도 하나는 알겠다. 이정룡이 이곳에 온 이유는 사과가 아니라는 것.
240|
241|아득한 힘의 차이를 각인시킨 그는 만족스럽게 웃으며 말을 이었다.
242|
243|“그리고 병문안 온 손님에게 이러면 안 되지. 특히 환자를 위한 선물까지 가져온 손님한테는. 안 그런가, 석 팀장?”
244|
245|“맞습니다. 부길드장님.”
246|
247|로봇처럼 대답한 석고준이 문을 두드렸다. 밖에서 대기하고 있던 경호팀 소속 헌터 하나가 들어와 손에 든 것을 탁자에 올려놨다.
248|
249|수백 송이의 꽃이 담긴 화병. 그리고 한 장의 봉투.
250|
251|“위로금일세. 액수가 부족하면 얼마든지 말하게.”
252|
253|내 시선은 꽃에 고정되어 있었다. 아름답고, 희었다. 평소 꽃을 좋아하는 건 아니지만 싫어하지도 않았던 나다.
254|
255|하지만 선물 받은 꽃을 보고 기분이 더럽기는 난생처음이었다.
256|
257|‘병문안 선물이 백합이라.’
258|
259|잊고 있던 분노가 스멀스멀 기어오른다.
260|
261|나는 뻐근하게 저려 오는 뒷목을 주무르며 중얼거렸다.
262|
263|“이런 개 같은 노인네를 봤나…….”
264|
265|이번만큼은 석고준도 참지 않았다. 괴성과 함께 달려든 놈의 주먹이 눈부신 속도로 내 아래턱을 후려갈겼다.
266|
267|뻑!
268|
269|섬뜩한 소리와 함께 피가 튀었다.
270|
271|나는 눈살을 찌푸리며 기울어진 고개를 천천히 돌렸다. 입 안에서 끈적하고 짭짤한 피 맛이 느껴졌다.
272|
273|“젠장. 혀 깨물었잖아.”
274|
275|석고준이 눈을 부릅떴다. 놈은 믿을 수 없다는 듯한 눈빛으로 자신의 주먹과 나를 번갈아 봤다.
276|
277|“어떻게?”
278|
279|“내가 좀 튼튼해. 어릴 때부터 우유를 많이 마셔서.”
280|
281|“분명히 마나를 실었는데…….”
282|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P103]
Though my heart had cried out for anger and revenge, I had never expected Lee Jungryong to come. Even in the midst of that rage, my mind had coldly compromised with reality.

[P104]
*Lee Jungryong, the man who effectively ruled Ares Guild, was still a giant I couldn’t force to his knees with my current strength.*

[P105]
“A demand is the right of the strong. Words spoken by the weak to the strong can never be demands. They are always requests—or invitations.”

[P106]
“……!”

[P107]
“That’s why I came in response to an invitation. Whatever leverage you think you have over me, that fact will not change. I am Lee Jungryong. I am Ares Guild, and Ares Guild is me.”

[P108]
His voice was quiet, but it carried weight. Everyone in the Peace Guild, myself included, was left speechless.

[P109]
At least one thing was clear.

[P110]
Lee Jungryong hadn’t come here to apologize.

[P111]
Having driven the overwhelming difference in our power into our minds, he continued with a satisfied smile.

[P112]
“And this is no way to treat a guest who came to visit a patient. Especially one who brought a gift for him. Isn’t that right, Team Leader Seok?”

[P113]
“That is correct, Vice Guild Master.”

[P114]
Go Jun answered like a robot and knocked on the door. A Hunter from the security team who had been waiting outside entered and placed what he was carrying on the table.

[P115]
A vase filled with hundreds of flowers.

[P116]
And an envelope.

[P117]
“Compensation money. If the amount isn’t enough, tell me. I’ll give you as much as you need.”

[P118]
My gaze remained fixed on the flowers. They were beautiful and white. I had never been particularly fond of flowers, but I had never disliked them, either.

[P119]
Yet this was the first time in my life that receiving flowers as a gift had made me feel disgusted.

[P120]
*Lilies as a hospital-visit gift.*

[P121]
My dormant anger began crawling back up from the depths.

[P122]
I rubbed the stiff, tingling back of my neck and muttered,

[P123]
“What a fucking old bastard…”

[P124]
This time, even Go Jun couldn’t restrain himself.

[P125]
With a roar, he charged. His fist slammed into my lower jaw at blinding speed.

[P126]
Crack!

[P127]
Blood sprayed with a sickening sound.

[P128]
I frowned and slowly turned my head back into place. The sticky, salty taste of blood filled my mouth.

[P129]
“Damn it. I bit my tongue.”

[P130]
Go Jun’s eyes widened. He looked back and forth between his fist and me as though he couldn’t believe what he was seeing.

[P131]
“How?”

[P132]
“I’m pretty tough. I drank a lot of milk when I was young.”

[P133]
“I definitely imbued it with mana…”

[P134]
If it had been fully materialized Fist Energy, I wouldn’t still be standing here like this.

[P135]
Of course, if that had been the case, I wouldn’t have deliberately let him hit me, either.

[P136]
I flashed him a grin.

[P137]
“You should have used everything you had. Enough to finish me in one blow.”

[P138]
Whoosh!

[P139]
“Hup!”

[P140]
My arm shot out. Go Jun sucked in a short breath and reached to knock it aside, moving at a speed no ordinary A-rank Hunter could hope to match.

[P141]
His hand curved like a hook as it snapped toward my wrist.

[P142]
*This really is a grappling technique.*

[P143]
Remembering the surprise I had felt while fighting Park Jihoon, I smoothly twisted my wrist.

[P144]
Slip.

[P145]
His hand clawed through empty air. I wound around his wrist, locked it in place, and put my weight into a stomp that crashed down onto the top of his foot.

[P146]
Crack!

[P147]
“Urgh!”

[P148]
The weight of a thousand geun crushed Go Jun’s instep and drove it deep into the solid concrete. Groaning in pain, he raised his arm to shield his face.

[P149]
But…

[P150]
“You think that’ll do?”

[P151]
One thing was certain.

[P152]
I hadn’t avoided his blow.

[P153]
Go Jun hadn’t been able to avoid mine.

[P154]
Crunch!

[P155]
My fist struck the exact center of his face, breaking his nose in one blow and caving in the flesh beneath it.

[P156]
His mouth gaped open, spraying blood and white teeth.

[P157]
Clatter. Thud.

[P158]
“Fucking bastard. Who said you could throw the first punch?”

[P159]
“……!”

[P160]
It all happened in an instant. Everyone in the hospital room was shocked, but one person’s reaction stood out in particular.

[P161]
“You bastard…”

[P162]
The voice that had remained relaxed throughout trembled faintly. Ripples spread through Lee Jungryong’s eyes.

[P163]
I quickly spoke first, before things could get worse.

[P164]
“For the record, that was self-defense.”

[P165]
But the words I heard next were something I could never have anticipated.

[P166]
“What is your relationship with my older brother?”

[P167]
“Excuse me? Who?”

[P168]
“The person who taught you that.”

[P169]
“If you mean that…”

[P170]
My eyes widened.

[P171]
*Was this old man talking about martial arts?*

[P172]
But Lee Jungryong was no longer listening to me. His gaze had turned cold and heavy as he stared at Team Leader Choi.

[P173]
“Did Soyeong have another man?”

[P174]
I didn’t know who Soyeong was.

[P175]
But to someone else, that name was apparently a dragon’s reverse scale—a point that must never be touched.

[P176]
Team Leader Choi clenched his fists, and blue flames blazed in Butler Kim’s eyes.

[P177]
“Senior. Do you want to die?”

[P178]
“Answer me.”

[P179]
“You bastard! Lee Jungryong!”

[P180]
“Now.”

[P181]
That was when Team Leader Choi’s tightly sealed lips finally parted.

[P182]
“You know better than I do what kind of relationship those two had.”

[P183]
“Then that bastard…”

[P184]
“You must have already investigated Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P185]
“Are you saying all of it is true?”

[P186]
“It is exactly as you know it. There isn’t a single lie.”

[P187]
Lee Jungryong’s eyes trembled.

[P188]
After looking back and forth between Team Leader Choi and me, he finally turned away. The door opened as though someone had been waiting for the signal, but he came to an abrupt stop before leaving.

[P189]
He tossed out a single sentence.

[P190]
“I’ll send someone soon. Once the negotiations are over, hand over the people you’re holding.”

[P191]
Click.

[P192]
The door closed behind the last person to leave—the security team Hunter carrying Go Jun on his back.

[P193]
It felt as though a storm had just swept through the room.

[P194]
I turned toward Team Leader Choi, who was silently staring at the tightly closed door.

[P195]
“Who is Soyeong?”

[P196]
“She was my mother.”

[P197]
“……What?”

[P198]
“The mother who gave birth to me and raised me. She passed away a long time ago.”

[P199]
My mouth fell open despite myself.

[P200]
*What the hell is wrong with that old man?*

[P201]
He had asked a man to his face whether his late mother had cheated while she was alive.

[P202]
“Crazy. Why would he—ah, never mind. You don’t have to answer.”

[P203]
“Vice Guild Master Lee must have been quite shaken. Even I didn’t expect him to ask so directly.”

[P204]
*To hell with whether he was shaken.*

[P205]
I frantically waved my hands.

[P206]
“Team Leader, really, it’s fine. You don’t have to tell me.”

[P207]
“Sometimes I wonder what it would have been like if my mother had been born as someone other than Cheon Taemin’s daughter.”

[P208]
“All right, that’s enough…”

[P209]
My body abruptly froze.

[P210]
*What did he just say?*

[P211]
Although I couldn’t move an inch, my mind repeated those three syllables faster than ever.

[P212]
*Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin…*

[P213]
“Did you just say Cheon Taemin?”

[P214]
“If my pronunciation wasn’t incorrect, then you heard me correctly.”

[P215]
“Could it be… the Cheon Taemin I know?”

[P216]
“Yes.”

[P217]
Team Leader Choi nodded and continued.

[P218]
“He was my maternal grandfather.”

[P219]
For a moment, my vision spun and my legs wobbled.

[P220]
*Cheon Taemin. He said Cheon Taemin.*

[P221]
I had once harbored doubts about Team Leader Choi’s identity.

[P222]
A man in his twenties with seemingly limitless ability, whom an A-rank mage known as a hidden hero of the Great Cataclysm called Young Master.

[P223]
Now I finally understood how all of that had been possible.

[P224]
It was because his maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin.

[P225]
*Humanity’s great hero. The world’s greatest Hunter…*

[P226]
Among all the words used to describe Cheon Taemin, the title “Guild Master of Ares Guild” was only one small piece.

[P227]
The largest piece was an immortal feat no one else had ever achieved.

[P228]
*The man who killed the Demon King. The Slayer.*

[P229]
And Cheon Taemin’s own grandson was standing right in front of me.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 287

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃287화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|나, 임꺽정, 송송이와 김 집사.
  6|
  7|그러나 병실로 들어선 이정룡의 시선은 오직 한 사람에게 고정되어 있었다.
  8|
  9|바로 최 팀장이었다.
 10|
 11|“많이 컸구나.”
 12|
 13|“……!”
 14|
 15|이정룡의 첫 마디를 듣는 순간, 쇠망치로 뒤통수를 한 대 맞은 듯한 기분이 들었다.
 16|
 17|이거였다. 최 팀장이 숨긴 것이.
 18|
 19|직장 상사와의 단순한 상하 관계가 아닌 게 분명했다.
 20|
 21|‘내가 알기로 최 팀장이 아레스 길드에 몸담았던 기간은 삼사 년 남짓.’
 22|
 23|아무리 적게 잡아도 이십 대 초중반 때 이정룡을 만났을 것이다. 그런 그에게 많이 컸다는 말은 어울리지 않는다.
 24|
 25|그건 부모님 친구나 명절날 친척들에게서나 듣는 소리니까.
 26|
 27|“오랜만에 뵙습니다. 이정룡 부길드장님.”
 28|
 29|딱딱한 호칭과 말투. 이정룡이 흥미롭다는 눈빛으로 최 팀장을 응시했다.
 30|
 31|“부길드장님이라, 네가 어렸을 때는 나를 할아버지라 불렀었지.”
 32|
 33|할아버지라고?
 34|
 35|두 번째 충격이다. 순간 혹시? 하는 생각이 들었지만 이내 머릿속에서 지웠다.
 36|
 37|이건 단순한 호칭 문제다. 어린 마음에 할아버지라 불렀을 뿐, 이정룡이 최 팀장의 진짜 할아버지는 아닐 것이다.
 38|
 39|‘최 팀장이 어렸을 때부터 긴밀한 관계가 있었던 건 확실해 보이는데.’
 40|
 41|이정룡과 그런 사이였다는 것만으로도 이미 보통이 아니다.
 42|
 43|모두가 놀라는 가운데 평정심을 유지하고 있는 사람은 김 집사와 침착하게 대답하는 최 팀장뿐이었다.
 44|
 45|“그랬었지요. 20년 전에는.”
 46|
 47|“세월이 무섭구나. 그렇게 애교 많던 꼬마 녀석이 이렇게 변할 줄이야.”
 48|
 49|“갈수록 보이지 않던 것들이 점점 보이더군요.”
 50|
 51|“작년에 사표를 냈다는 보고는 받았다. 곰곰이 생각해 보니 네가 길드에 들어온 후 얼굴 한 번 본 적 없더구나. 내심 아쉽다는 생각이 들었지.”
 52|
 53|말과는 달리 전혀 아쉬운 표정이 아니다. 대답하는 최 팀장 역시 마찬가지였다.
 54|
 55|“저도 마찬가집니다. 본사에는 발도 들이지 못하게 바로 해외 발령만 안 내셨다면 자주 뵐 수 있었을 텐데요.”
 56|
 57|“왜, 해외 지사가 마음에 들지 않더냐?”
 58|
 59|“제가 있을 곳이 아니라고 느꼈습니다. 그뿐입니다.”
 60|
 61|“있을 곳이 아니다…….”
 62|
 63|“부길드장님께서도 원하신 그림 아닙니까?”
 64|
 65|“내가 말이냐?”
 66|
 67|이정룡이 피식, 웃음을 터트렸다.
 68|
 69|“그래서 새 둥지를 틀었느냐? 남의 이름을 빌려 가면서까지?”
 70|
 71|“말씀하시는데 끼어들어 죄송합니다만.”
 72|
 73|침묵을 지키고 있던 김 집사가 불쑥 입을 열었다. 평소처럼 평온하기 그지없는 목소리다.
 74|
 75|“도련님과 제가 남은 아니지요.”
 76|
 77|“아니, 이게 누군가?”
 78|
 79|이정룡이 짐짓 눈을 크게 떴다.
 80|
 81|다분히 과장된 행동이었다. 최 팀장을 알았다면 그와 가장 가까운 김 집사를 모를 리 없을 테니까.
 82|
 83|“김화종? 화종이 맞지?”
 84|

[P25]

[P26]

[P27]
“I felt the same way. If you hadn’t immediately transferred me overseas and barred me from even setting foot in headquarters, we might have seen each other more often.”

[P29]
“I felt it wasn’t where I belonged. That’s all.”

[P30]
“Not where you belonged…”

[P31]
“Wasn’t that exactly what you wanted, Vice Guild Master?”

[P32]
“Me?”

[P33]
Lee Jungryong let out a quiet laugh.

[P34]

[P35]
“I’m sorry to interrupt.”

[P36]

[P37]

[P38]
“Oh, who might this be?”

Lee Jungryong widened his eyes in feigned surprise.

[P42]

*Informal speech? And Senior?*

*Ah. So it wasn’t my imagination.*

Close, my ass. I must have been blind.

He fucking hated him. Enough to wish he had died.

[P82]

[P89]

[P91]
To Park Jihoon and Park Tae Seop.

[P95]
*Thank him?*

[P104]
*Lee Jungryong, the man who effectively ruled Ares Guild, was still a giant I couldn’t force to his knees with my current strength.*

At least one thing was clear.

Lee Jungryong hadn’t come here to apologize.

[P115]
A vase filled with hundreds of flowers.

[P119]
Yet this was the first time in my life that receiving flowers as a gift had made me feel disgusted.

[P120]
*Lilies as a hospital-visit gift.*

[P121]
My dormant anger began crawling back up from the depths.

[P122]
I rubbed the stiff, tingling back of my neck and muttered,

[P123]
“What a fucking old bastard…”

[P124]
This time, even Go Jun couldn’t restrain himself.

[P125]
With a roar, he charged. His fist slammed into my lower jaw at blinding speed.

[P126]
Crack!

[P127]
Blood sprayed with a sickening sound.

[P128]
I frowned and slowly turned my head back into place. The sticky, salty taste of blood filled my mouth.

[P129]
“Damn it. I bit my tongue.”

[P130]
Go Jun’s eyes widened. He looked back and forth between his fist and me as though he couldn’t believe what he was seeing.

[P131]
“How?”

[P132]
“I’m pretty tough. I drank a lot of milk when I was young.”

[P133]
“I definitely imbued it with mana…”

[P134]
If it had been fully materialized Fist Energy, I wouldn’t still be standing here like this.

[P135]
Of course, if that had been the case, I wouldn’t have deliberately let him hit me, either.

[P136]
I flashed him a grin.

[P137]
“You should have used everything you had. Enough to finish me in one blow.”

[P138]
Whoosh!

[P139]
“Hup!”

[P140]
My arm shot out. Go Jun sucked in a short breath and reached to knock it aside, moving at a speed no ordinary A-rank Hunter could hope to match.

[P141]
His hand curved like a hook as it snapped toward my wrist.

[P142]
*This really is a grappling technique.*

[P143]
Remembering the surprise I had felt while fighting Park Jihoon, I smoothly twisted my wrist.

[P144]
Slip.

[P145]
His hand clawed through empty air. I wound around his wrist, locked it in place, and put my weight into a stomp that crashed down onto the top of his foot.

[P146]
Crack!

[P147]
“Urgh!”

[P148]
The weight of a thousand geun crushed Go Jun’s instep and drove it deep into the solid concrete. Groaning in pain, he raised his arm to shield his face.

[P149]
But…

[P150]
“You think that’ll do?”

[P151]
One thing was certain.

[P152]
I hadn’t avoided his blow.

[P153]
Go Jun hadn’t been able to avoid mine.

[P154]
Crunch!

[P155]
My fist struck the exact center of his face, breaking his nose in one blow and caving in the flesh beneath it.

[P156]
His mouth gaped open, spraying blood and white teeth.

[P157]
Clatter. Thud.

[P158]
“Fucking bastard. Who said you could throw the first punch?”

[P159]
“……!”

[P160]
It all happened in an instant. Everyone in the hospital room was shocked, but one person’s reaction stood out in particular.

[P161]
“You bastard…”

[P162]
The voice that had remained relaxed throughout trembled faintly. Ripples spread through Lee Jungryong’s eyes.

[P163]
I quickly spoke first, before things could get worse.

[P164]
“For the record, that was self-defense.”

[P165]
But the words I heard next were something I could never have anticipated.

[P166]
“What is your relationship with my older brother?”

[P167]
“Excuse me? Who?”

[P168]
“The person who taught you that.”

[P169]
“If you mean that…”

[P170]
My eyes widened.

[P171]
*Was this old man talking about martial arts?*

[P172]
But Lee Jungryong was no longer listening to me. His gaze had turned cold and heavy as he stared at Team Leader Choi.

[P173]
“Did Soyeong have another man?”

[P174]
I didn’t know who Soyeong was.

[P175]
But to someone else, that name was apparently a dragon’s reverse scale—a point that must never be touched.

[P176]
Team Leader Choi clenched his fists, and blue flames blazed in Butler Kim’s eyes.

[P177]
“Senior. Do you want to die?”

[P178]
“Answer me.”

[P179]
“You bastard! Lee Jungryong!”

[P180]
“Now.”

[P181]
That was when Team Leader Choi’s tightly sealed lips finally parted.

[P182]
“You know better than I do what kind of relationship those two had.”

[P183]
“Then that bastard…”

[P184]
“You must have already investigated Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P185]
“Are you saying all of it is true?”

[P186]
“It is exactly as you know it. There isn’t a single lie.”

[P187]
Lee Jungryong’s eyes trembled.

[P188]
After looking back and forth between Team Leader Choi and me, he finally turned away. The door opened as though someone had been waiting for the signal, but he came to an abrupt stop before leaving.

[P189]
He tossed out a single sentence.

[P190]
“I’ll send someone soon. Once the negotiations are over, hand over the people you’re holding.”

[P191]
Click.

[P192]
The door closed behind the last person to leave—the security team Hunter carrying Go Jun on his back.

[P193]
It felt as though a storm had just swept through the room.

[P194]
I turned toward Team Leader Choi, who was silently staring at the tightly closed door.

[P195]
“Who is Soyeong?”

[P196]
“She was my mother.”

[P197]
“……What?”

[P198]
“The mother who gave birth to me and raised me. She passed away a long time ago.”

[P199]
My mouth fell open despite myself.

[P200]
*What the hell is wrong with that old man?*

[P201]
He had asked a man to his face whether his late mother had cheated while she was alive.

[P202]
“Crazy. Why would he—ah, never mind. You don’t have to answer.”

[P203]
“Vice Guild Master Lee must have been quite shaken. Even I didn’t expect him to ask so directly.”

[P204]
*To hell with whether he was shaken.*

[P205]
I frantically waved my hands.

[P206]
“Team Leader, really, it’s fine. You don’t have to tell me.”

[P207]
“Sometimes I wonder what it would have been like if my mother had been born as someone other than Cheon Taemin’s daughter.”

[P208]
“All right, that’s enough…”

[P209]
My body abruptly froze.

[P210]
*What did he just say?*

[P211]
Although I couldn’t move an inch, my mind repeated those three syllables faster than ever.

[P212]
*Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin…*

[P213]
“Did you just say Cheon Taemin?”

[P214]
“If my pronunciation wasn’t incorrect, then you heard me correctly.”

[P215]
“Could it be… the Cheon Taemin I know?”

[P216]
“Yes.”

[P217]
Team Leader Choi nodded and continued.

[P218]
“He was my maternal grandfather.”

[P219]
For a moment, my vision spun and my legs wobbled.

[P220]
*Cheon Taemin. He said Cheon Taemin.*

[P221]
I had once harbored doubts about Team Leader Choi’s identity.

[P222]
A man in his twenties with seemingly limitless ability, whom an A-rank mage known as a hidden hero of the Great Cataclysm called Young Master.

[P223]
Now I finally understood how all of that had been possible.

[P224]
It was because his maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin.

[P225]
*Humanity’s great hero. The world’s greatest Hunter…*

[P226]
Among all the words used to describe Cheon Taemin, the title “Guild Master of Ares Guild” was only one small piece.

[P227]
The largest piece was an immortal feat no one else had ever achieved.

[P228]
*The man who killed the Demon King. The Slayer.*

[P229]
And Cheon Taemin’s own grandson was standing right in front of me.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
